title: Budget Billing Enrollment Acceptance Standards
content:
# Budget Billing Enrollment Acceptance Standards

**Standard.** Enrollment in a Budget Billing plan is accepted only on a service agreement in active status. The agreement's schedule must be among the plan's eligible rate schedules, a business agreement's highest measured demand in its last 12 bills may not exceed the plan's demand limit, and a FlatBill requires the plan's minimum months of service, 12-month usage no more than the plan's annual usage cap and no net metering agreement in approved or operating status. The past-due balance may not exceed the plan's largest past-due balance allowed at enrollment, except that arrears placed in an active payment arrangement are disregarded where the plan disregards such arrears. Plans that may not be held on a time-of-use schedule are not held on time-of-use schedules. Enrollment is the customer's own choice and takes effect on the plan's first plan bill, the first regular bill issued after enrollment.

The plan-by-plan figures each condition reads — eligible schedules, demand limit, usage cap, months of service, past-due allowance and the treatment of arrangement arrears — are those set for the plan the customer chooses.

## Agreement status

The status test is decided on the company's service agreement record for the agreement being enrolled, as it stands before the enrollment is made; a customer's statement about the account does not replace it.

| Agreement status on record | Enrollment |
|---|---|
| Active | May be accepted, subject to the other conditions |
| Notice pending | Not accepted |
| Disconnected | Not accepted |
| Closed | Not accepted |

## Conditions by plan family

| Condition | Residential Levelized and Budget Billing Plans | Commercial Levelized and Budget Billing Plans | Residential FlatBill Plan and Small Business FlatBill Plan |
|---|---|---|---|
| Agreement in active status | Required | Required | Required |
| Schedule among the plan's eligible schedules | Required | Required | Required |
| Highest measured demand in the last 12 bills within the plan's demand limit | — (residential) | Required | Required for the Small Business FlatBill Plan (business) |
| Plan's minimum months of service at the address | — | — | Required |
| 12-month usage no more than the plan's annual usage cap | — | — | Required |
| No net metering agreement in approved or operating status | — | — | Required |
| Past-due balance within the plan's allowance | Required; arrears in an active payment arrangement disregarded | Required; arrears in an active payment arrangement disregarded | Required; arrears in an active payment arrangement counted |
| Not on a time-of-use schedule | — | — | Required |

## Hypothetical cases

1. A residential customer on Schedule RS with 14 months of service, 31,200 kWh of usage over the last 12 months, no past-due balance and a net metering agreement in operating status asks for the Residential FlatBill Plan. The net metering agreement in operating status prevents the FlatBill enrollment. The Residential Budget Billing Plan is not subject to that condition.
2. A business customer on Schedule GD whose agreement status is notice pending asks for the Commercial Levelized Billing Plan. The agreement is not in active status, and the enrollment is not accepted, whatever the other conditions show.
3. A residential customer on Schedule RT, active, with $210.00 of arrears all placed in an active payment arrangement asks for the Residential Levelized Billing Plan. The arrangement arrears are disregarded, the past-due balance counted is $0.00, and the enrollment meets the past-due condition.
4. The same customer asks instead for the Residential FlatBill Plan. Schedule RT is a time-of-use schedule and is not among the FlatBill plan's eligible schedules, and the arrangement arrears are counted; the enrollment is not accepted.

## Choice and effect

Choosing a plan is the customer's own decision. The plan installment first appears on the first regular bill issued after enrollment, and the plan becomes active when that bill is issued.
